about.title: Personal Injury Help in Tustin, California
about.longDescription: Tustin sits at a busy meeting point of Orange County traffic. The I-5 runs along its edge, Jamboree Road carries commuters toward Irvine, and Red Hill Avenue and Newport Avenue thread past neighborhoods, shopping centers, and the Old Town district. Public records for 2025 list 328 injury collisions inside the city, with 441 people hurt and 5 lives lost. Four corridors — I-5 Northbound, Red Hill Avenue, Newport Avenue, and Jamboree Road — appear most often in those counts, and reports tend to bunch up on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when the evening drive is at its heaviest. Behind each number is someone sorting out medical bills, missed shifts, and phone calls from an insurer they never asked to hear from. That is where LawProactive comes in. We are a free service, not a law firm. We do not represent you ourselves; we connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who can. Attorneys in our network take cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. A short conversation can help you understand where you stand before California's two-year filing window starts to close.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Tustin Claim

items.title: Two years to act — sometimes far less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some blame for a collision on Jamboree Road, your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you are not shut out.

items.title: No cap on pain-and-suffering damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not limit non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. Your claim is evaluated on what actually happened to you.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency. You pay nothing up front, and there is no attorney fee unless money is recovered for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Tustin?
items.answer: For most injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date you were hurt. If a government entity is involved — say, a city vehicle or a hazard on public property — you may need to file an administrative claim within six months. Because the clock is different depending on who is responsible, it helps to have the facts sorted out early.

items.question: Where do Tustin crashes tend to happen, according to public records?
items.answer: Collision counts for Tustin are highest along I-5 Northbound, Red Hill Avenue, Newport Avenue, and Jamboree Road. In 2025 the city recorded 328 injury collisions, 441 people injured, and 5 traffic deaths, with reports peaking on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are simply public-record tallies of where and when crashes were reported.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the collision?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means being partially responsible reduces your recovery rather than eliminating it. If you are found 20 percent at fault, for example, your compensation is reduced by 20 percent. An attorney can help make sure the fault assigned to you is fair and supported by the evidence.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive?

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company first?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to another party's insurer, and what you say can be used to minimize your claim. Many people choose to speak with an attorney before returning those calls. That conversation is free, and it can help you understand your rights before you commit to anything.
